text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt and Syria move to prepare joint Arab market as first step towards new stage in Arab relations. Mubarak discussed with Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam and Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara obstcles placed by Israel in the way of the peace process and Turkey's incursion into Iraq.
- OAU summit opens in Harare. Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to meet Mandela, Kabila, Mugabe and other African leaders.
- Important talks for Mubarak and Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah who starts visit to Egypt today.
- Cabinet to discuss in meeting on Wednesday ways to encourage exports and Egyptian-European partnership and to follow up work at New Valley Delta project.
- Presidential adviser Osama el-Baz says Egypt's goal is to narrow gap between parties in order to take peace process out of crisis.
- Census shows that Egypt's population totals 61.5 million and that population development had decreased by 0.07 percent.
- Judicial source says that Asharq al-Awsat published lies about Alaa and Gamal Mubarak.
- Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar explains to U.S. ambassador the Islamic basis of call to execution of those who sell land to Jews.
- Public Enterprise minister says government will not increase prices of popular medicines or those for chronic illnesses.
- Industry minister says Egypt turned down Israel's request to import Egyptian coal.
- Mubarak in telephone conversations with Jordan's King Hussein and Turkey's Erbakan.
- Interior Ministry says confiscation of books follows judiciary decree.
